sla_negotiation_points: Throughput guarantee: baseline 1,200 rps sustained, bursts to 5,000 rps for 10m windows.
Latency SLO: 95th percentile generation < 120ms for short-context chat (<=128 tokens); 99th percentile SLA tied to incident credits.
Availability: 99.95% per-month for dedicated pools; credits for regional failover events >5 minutes.
Penalty model: service credits capped at 20% of monthly fee; customer requested higher for multi-hour outages — negotiating.
Support: 24/7 Pager for severity 1, dedicated TAM for onboarding window (first 90 days).
capacity_requirements: Baseline reserved: 8x A100 80GB (reserved) with autoscale burst pool of +2 nodes for traffic spikes.
Expected baseline throughput: ~1,200 rps for small chat requests or 3-4k rerank ops/sec depending on batching.
KV/prefix cache: needs cross-region replication for hot prefixes with eventual consistency; want TTL tuning recommendations.
Batching policy: continuous batching for embeddings, strict latency-first batching for live-rerank paths.
fallback_design_summary: Primary strategy: active region (us-east-1) with warm passive region (us-west-2). Health checks at infra + model-level (p99 latency and queue depth).
Model-variant fallback: prefer quantized 7B (Q4_0) for overflow path; route to 13B float only when quality-critical and capacity available. Auto-toggle via rollout policies with telemetry flags.

Saturation handling: when queue depth > threshold OR estimated token latency breach, perform staged degradation: 1) enable tighter batching (preserve throughput), 2) route subset traffic to quantized variant, 3) enable shared-hosted fallback with tagging and rate limits.

Cross-region constraints: PII must be masked before cross-region failover. Implement token scrubbing and KMS key usage to enforce residency policy. Legal team to sign off on last-resort shared-host fallback.
Operational playbook: runbook drafted (link in Drive). Weekly DR drills during onboarding window; post-drill telemetry checklist (trace ids, request sampling, cache hit rates).
